chapter_title: Concerning the Three Things that were established

fills.fill: and they placed the fetter beneath
fills.notes: The sentence explains the new luminous earth as a superposed structure; in the substrate logic it is the upper ‘earth’ laid over the lower as a binding-layer. A clause about placing/setting a fetter or foundation beneath fits the necessity-theme (binding the Enemy) and prepares for the next apposition (“namely that alien body … built upon it”).
After “that alien body” the verb “built upon it” requires a subject; the simplest old-layer connective is a relative clause resuming the agents (“they”) who fashion the binding structures.

fills.fill: bring together the dark fire into it
fills.notes: Second necessity: the ‘coffin’ is defined as containment of the dark fire. The substrate sequence is: gather/collect → shut in → bind. “Bring together … into it” supplies the mechanical, impersonal operation appropriate to the cosmological register.
Pairs with the prior gathering: once collected, it is enclosed. “Shut in” matches the coffin/prison imagery without moralizing.

Apposition: “the new earth, the coffin … of the dark fire” naturally expands with a second title. In this teaching-layer the coffin is simultaneously the prison prepared for the hostile power and its fire.

fills.fill: set to lamentation, and there is
fills.notes: The line needs a predicate leading into “woe”; the oldest-layer idiom is an assignment to a state (lamentation) rather than exhortation. “Set to lamentation” frames “woe” as their fixed condition under judgment by deed.

The ‘rag/mat/footstool’ are said to be for ‘this coffin … which is the prison of the enemy’; that coffin was identified in ¶4 with the new earth. Restoring “of the new earth” tightens the correspondence: the sinners’ forms become the lowest serviceable layer of the enclosing earth/coffin.

assessment: Most gaps can be constrained by the correspondential mechanics of the passage: three ‘necessities’ that function as binding/containment structures separating Darkness from the Enemy. Exact verbs in ¶4–¶5 remain somewhat fluid (gather/enclose/appoint-to-lament), but the required operations (collect → shut in → imprison; condemn → crucify upon the Enemy; make a lowest layer serving the coffin/new earth) are tight.
